subject: Legend not inheriting the alpha values

messages.author: 6d1cd0a71e6148df
messages.subject: Legend not inheriting the alpha values
parts:
Hi!

Is it possible to make the legend *not* inherit the alpha values of the
geoms? I frequently plot data on rather large datasets, where I have to
use a low value of alpha to avoid overplotting issues. The actual plot
looks good, but the legend becomes unreadable, as the alpha value make
the colour of a single geom almost transparent.

Here's a simple example:

qplot(x,z,data=diamonds, colour=cut, alpha=I(1/40))+xlim(4,10)+ylim(0,10)

(My preferred way of ggplot2 handling this would be to automatically
*not* inherit the alpha value when *setting* it, only when mapping it.)

--
Karl Ove Hufthammer

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Legend not inheriting the alpha values
parts:
Hi,

Perhaps you can trick ggplot2 by adding a dummy layer,

ggplot()+
geom_point(data=diamonds,map=aes(x,z,colour=cut),alpha=1/40)+
xlim(4,10)+
ylim(0,10) +
geom_point(data=subset(diamonds, FALSE),map=aes(NA,NA,colour=cut))


HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Legend not inheriting the alpha values
parts:
Hi Karl,

Hmmm, I have thought about that in the past. The problem comes with
legends for (e.g.) geom_smooth - if you ignore the alpha, then the
smoother doesn't match the plot. I wonder if only using alpha for
fill colour in legends would work.

Hadley
